angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 8,913,308 km at 49.55 pc = 2.4 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 19780: distance 49.554 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.005), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 49.554 +/- 0.248 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 20.3431 +/- 0.1859 mas (same row, RUWE 4.09), 109.4 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 12.812 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 19780: radius 12.812 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 103.911 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.049) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 8,913,308 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5152 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 19780: effective temperature 5152 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.04) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 19780: effective temperature 5152 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.04) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * alf Ret: spectral type G8IIIa: (1989ApJS...71..245K)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * alf Ret: projected rotation speed 4.7 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Burnashev (1985), Abastumani Astrophys. Obs. Bull. 59, 83; VizieR III/126, part2 record 35 (BS 1336), cross-checked against Gaia DR3 XP spectrum, source 4676528209144882304 (41 levels apart at most, the threshold is 12)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.56 from 2024A&A...690A..97C; the 7 published values span log g 2.39 to 3.03, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.2% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...690A..97C)
